name: Great Pyramid of Giza
headline: height
subtitle: Pyramid of Khufu, Giza, Egypt
description: The Great Pyramid is the largest of the three pyramids on the Giza plateau west of the Nile, built for the 4th-dynasty king Khufu (Cheops) and finished in the early 25th century BCE. It was originally about 147 m tall, but erosion and the loss of most of its smooth limestone casing have brought it down to about 137 m. Each side of its square base is about 230 m long, and its faces slope at 51.87 degrees.

measures.label: Current height
measures.note: Present height after erosion and removal of most of the casing stones (Britannica gives 449 ft)

measures.label: Original height
measures.note: Height when the polished limestone casing was complete (Britannica gives about 482 ft)

measures.label: Base side length
measures.note: Length of each side of the square base (Britannica gives 755 ft)

facts.text: Its faces rise at an angle of 51.87 degrees and are closely aligned to the four cardinal compass points.
About 2.3 million stone blocks were cut, moved and set in place to build it.
Its entrance is on the north face, about 18 m (59 ft) above the ground, and the corbelled Grand Gallery inside is 46 m (151 ft) long.
The Pyramids of Giza are the only one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world still standing.

caveats: Britannica gives the total weight as '5.75-million-ton' without saying whether short or metric tons are meant, so no mass is stored.
No volume figure was found in the fetched source, so volume is left out.
No Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities page with dimensions could be fetched; all figures come from Britannica.
